source_refs.note: Example 25.2.3 C₆H₅COCH₃ (acetophenone, TM): a main subheading of 25.2 Retrosynthesis and Synthesis of Some Compounds, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 137-139.

blocks.text: In first step the disconnection of acetophenone (TM) was done from C—C bond, which created synthons of aryl anion (C₆H₅⁻) and acylium (CH₃CO⁺) cation.

blocks.alt: Acetophenone (benzene with C(=O)CH3) with a wavy slash on the ring-carbon bond, a Disconnection arrow, then a negatively charged benzene ring, synthon (A), plus the acylium ion H3C-C(=O)+, synthon (B).
blocks.caption: Example 25.2.3, Step I: disconnection of acetophenone (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 138).

blocks.text: These synthons were neutralized to get synthetic equivalents i.e., benzene and acyl chloride molecule.

blocks.alt: Synthon (A) is equivalent to benzene (SE) and synthon (B) to acyl chloride, H3C-CO-Cl (SE).
blocks.caption: Example 25.2.3, Step II: synthetic equivalents (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 138).

blocks.text: Synthesis of acetophenone can be done by reaction between benzene and acyl chloride, in the presence of AlCl₃ as catalyst, using Friedel-Craft acylation process.

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: The landmark synthesis of cholesterol was first achieved in early 1950s by two competing groups headed each by Robert Robinson in Oxford and R.B. Woodward at Harvard. These synthetic schemes of cholesterol, had been previously predicted through biological studies.

blocks.prompt: a) Why nitration of benzene is done during synthesis of aniline?
blocks.explanation: An amino group cannot be put directly onto benzene, but a nitro group is easily introduced by electrophilic substitution (nitration). The nitro group is then reduced to NH₂ with Sn and HCl (an FGI).

blocks.alt: Phenyl ethanoate: a benzene ring (hexagon with a circle inside) joined at its upper-right corner to O; the O is joined to a C that carries CH3 to the upper right and a double bond down to O.
blocks.caption: Phenyl ethanoate, Quick Check 25.2 (original drawing after the textbook's structure).

blocks.prompt:
b) Phenyl ethanoate is an important molecule used in synthesis of medicines for hepatitis and various infection.
(i) Draw its retrosynthetic tree.
(ii) Write structures of its synthetic equivalents.
(iii) Design its linear synthesis.
blocks.explanation:
(i) Retrosynthetic tree: disconnect the C–O bond of the ester: CH₃COOC₆H₅ ⇒ CH₃CO⁺ (synthon A) + C₆H₅O⁻ (synthon B).
(ii) Synthetic equivalents: ethanoyl chloride (CH₃COCl) for CH₃CO⁺, and phenol (C₆H₅OH) for C₆H₅O⁻.
(iii) Linear synthesis: CH₃COCl + C₆H₅OH → CH₃COOC₆H₅ + HCl, in the presence of a base such as NaOH (phenol does not form the ester well with ethanoic acid itself).
